relationship: Editing and running Python lesson code connects a challenge prompt to console output and automated checking.

learnerLoop.action: Choose a lesson, edit or load code, run it and check the challenge.
learnerLoop.modelChange: The active program, runtime state and challenge progress change.
learnerLoop.evidence: The editor, console, status and checker feedback show what the code did.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Debug the program or progress to the next challenge.

invariants: Challenge feedback evaluates the current challenge code.
Console evidence belongs to the active program run.
safeAdaptations: Change lesson examples, prompts or starter code while retaining editable execution and challenge checking.
nonGoals: Serving as a general-purpose Python development environment.

task.description: Selected lesson question and current editable challenge.
task.visibility: Visible in the corresponding lesson, simulation or result state.

controls.description: Navigate lessons/examples/challenges, edit, execute, check and supply runtime input.
controls.visibility: Visible in the corresponding lesson, simulation or result state.

model.description: Read-only examples and editable syntax-highlighted Python.
model.visibility: Visible in the corresponding lesson, simulation or result state.

evidence.description: Runtime output, challenge status and retained completion count.
evidence.visibility: Visible in the corresponding lesson, simulation or result state.

source.description: Python program for the current challenge.
source.domain: 33 lessons with three challenges each; embedded offline Skulpt runtime.

input.domain: Values requested by the current program.

modes.views: Example code and Challenge 1/2/3; later challenges unlock after an attempt, not only a passing solution.
modes.persistence: Local progress and source persist; Export and Import transfer the saved work. Light/dark scheme retained.
modes.support: No Working toggle; examples and progressive challenge prompts provide existing support.

dependencies: Code input, highlight overlay and gutter use aligned typography and scrolling.
Run uses the embedded interpreter. Check evaluates supplied cases and applicable structural requirements; an attempt unlocks the next challenge.
Each lesson retains its own source, attempts and completion.
Run attention stops for the visit after running code or an example; introductory modal guides are absent.
implementation.completion: Individual challenges are marked completed by their existing checks; suite tracks 99 challenge completions.
limitations: Fixed checks are not proof of general program correctness. Embedded Skulpt is a teaching Python runtime, not unrestricted CPython.
